renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: pr_scatter
  title: Precision against recall per callset
  description: |-
    Each point is a callset compared with its truth set: its recall on the horizontal axis and its precision on the vertical axis, coloured by F1 and sized by the true positives it recovers. It answers which callset finds the most true variants without adding false ones.
    How to read: the top right corner is best, with every true variant found and no false call. A point far to the left misses true variants, a point low down adds false calls, so look at the false negative and false positive cards to see which one dominates.
    Lines and annotations: the curved contours are lines of equal F1, the harmonic mean of precision and recall, and the diagonal marks precision equal to recall. They are drawn from the definitions of the metrics, not from a cut-off.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30858580/ and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Illumina/hap.py/master/doc/happy.md
  kind: pr_benchmark
  roles:
    label: label
    recall: recall
    precision: precision
    f1: f1
    support: tp_comp

- component: advanced_viz
  id: confusion
  title: True and false calls per callset
  description: |-
    Each cell is a count of variants for one callset: the true positives, the false positives or the false negatives of its comparison with the truth set. It answers how many variants stand behind each precision and recall value.
    How to read: a callset with many more false negatives than false positives loses recall, and the reverse loses precision. Compare cells within a callset first, because callsets of different size are not comparable by raw count.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30858580/
  kind: confusion_matrix
  roles:
    label: label
    tp: tp_comp
    fp: fp
    fn: fn

- component: figure
  title: F1 score per callset
  description: |-
    Each bar is a callset, with its F1 score, the harmonic mean of its precision and recall, and a colour for the caller that made it. It answers which callset scores best overall.
    How to read: a short bar means either many missed variants or many false calls, so open the precision-recall tile to see which. Compare bars of the same truth set only.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median F1 score of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of RTG Tools.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30858580/ and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Illumina/hap.py/master/doc/happy.md
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: label
    y: f1
    color: caller
    labels:
      label: Callset
      f1: F1 score
      caller: Caller
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: f1

- component: card
  title: Best F1 score
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest F1 score among the callsets in view, and the box shows how all of them spread. It answers how good the best callset is and how far the others lag.
    How to read: a best score close to 1 means a callset that agrees with the truth set. A wide box means the callers differ a lot, so check which one is ahead before pooling them.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30858580/
  column: f1
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: best callset, with the spread

- component: table
  title: Benchmark table
  description: |-
    Each row is a callset compared with a truth set, with the caller, the true positives on both sides, the false positives and negatives, and the precision, recall and F1 derived from them. It answers the exact numbers behind every other tile.
    How to read: sort by F1, or filter by caller or truth set to compare like with like.

- component: card
  title: True positives by caller
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of true positives across the callsets in view, and the bars rank the callers by how many they recover. It answers which caller finds the most true variants.
    How to read: a caller far ahead recovers more of the truth set, but compare it with the false positive card, since a looser caller finds more of both.
  column: tp_comp
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: caller
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: true positives, by caller

- component: card
  title: Median F1 score
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median F1 score across the callsets in view, and the box shows their spread. It answers how accurate the benchmark is as a whole.
    How to read: a median near 1 means most callsets reproduce the truth set. A box that reaches far below the median points to a few weak callsets.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30858580/
  column: f1
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Precision
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average precision, the share of a callset's calls that are true, with the lowest and highest values across callsets. It answers how free of false calls the callsets are.
    How to read: a high average with a low minimum points to one callset adding false calls.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30858580/
  column: precision
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: grid
  caption: average precision, with its range

- component: card
  title: Recall
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median recall, the share of the truth set that a callset recovers, and the box shows the spread across callsets. It answers how much of the truth the callsets find.
    How to read: a low recall means missed variants, which the false negative card counts. The cited paper states no cut-off for recall, so none is drawn.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30858580/
  column: recall
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread

- component: card
  title: False positives
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total count of false positive calls across the callsets, and the box shows how they spread. It answers how many calls have no match in the truth set.
    How to read: a callset far above the rest is where precision is lost. Open the confusion matrix to compare it with its true positives.
  column: fp
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: total, with the spread across callsets

- component: card
  title: False negatives
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total count of truth variants that no callset found, and the histogram shows how they distribute across callsets. It answers how many true variants are missed.
    How to read: a pile of callsets near zero with a few far to the right means a few callers lose recall. Check those against the recall card.
  column: fn
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: total, with the distribution across callsets
